blind_clusters.strongest_cross_cutting_mechanism: One mechanism dominates, and it is not a topic: **a claim about the system and the system itself are maintained by two separate mechanisms, with nothing recomputing the claim at the moment it is relied on.** Clusters 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 — roughly 75 of the ~107 clustered findings — are all instances of it, differing only in which layer the orphaned copy lives on: prose vs the tree (PR body, ADR, README, runbook, TSDoc, frontmatter, ticket); a guard definition vs the executed path (library schema vs boot composition, hand-built JSON schema vs registered Zod shape, private walk vs shared discovery, CI gate vs pre-push); a check predicate vs the property it is cited for (Sonar vs logic, build-completion vs boot, listing vs read, readback vs effect); the test surface vs the code path; and GitHub's review state vs whether the defect was actually addressed. In every case the copy is green, cheap to write, and never re-derived, so the referent moves and the copy silently becomes a lie — which is also why the cures that held were all re-derivations (regenerating provenance from a pinned head, moving the refinement onto the boot path, a fail-loud generator check that halts when a constraint cannot propagate, mutation-testing the new candidate) rather than corrections. Three genuinely different generators account for most of the remainder and should not be folded in: error-state collapse at the point of failure (cluster 5), read-then-act across an unguarded window (cluster 6, which produces the filesystem TOCTOUs, the cancellation-ordering bugs and the two approve-then-reverse reversals alike), and shared-artefact collision from unowned parallel authorship (cluster 8). Cluster 9 (bot identity not a first-class principal) is a platform-topology mechanism that is upstream of, not an instance of, the dominant one — it is what forced the PR recreations that then discarded findings.

Of 27 bot review-thread findings I extracted, ~20 fit at least loosely; a non-trivial residue plainly does not, and it includes some of the window's heaviest items: PR743 "the PR controls the script that receives this `statuses: write` token" (privilege escalation); PR743 "a delayed redelivery for an older deployment can start after a newer run" (concurrency); PR747 `existsSync`/`readdirSync` TOCTOU (a race — and the report ITSELF elevates this as its top un-dispositioned residual in §3.2, so its headline new finding is not an instance of its own headline class); PR749 `process.exit(1)`-skips-`finally`; PR746 findings 2 and 4 — "Preserve the observability safety boundary before committing to a pre-config reporter" (design underspecification of a privacy invariant) and "Do build-vs-buy before bespoke shape" (method finding). §3.3's force-fit is the clearest tell: "the review surface we *read* is not the surface the findings *land on*" is a harvesting-coverage gap, not a record asserting what it does not derive.

(2) The compression hides cure-distinct sub-classes with OPPOSITE remedial arrows, which matters because §4.4 leans on the frame to conclude the estate's meta-programme is "validated". Sorting the ten by what actually cured them: (A) claim-not-derived — rows 9, 10, and row 3's first half; cure = derive the claim at write time. (B) enforcement declared off the execution path — rows 1, 2, 4, 7; cure = move the check onto the boot/codegen path plus a regression test (PR735 shipped a generation-time constraint audit; PR748 shipped `refineSentryLiveForPostHog`). (C) gate green against the wrong artefact — rows 5, 8; cure = reachability/scope meta-checks. (D) correct code, stale decision record — row 6 and ADR-163 §10; cure = amend the doc. In (B) the declaration is right and execution is missing; in (D) execution is right and the declaration is wrong. A ledger recording STATED vs CHECKED reaches roughly rows 7, 8, 9, 10 — about four of ten. It does not reach a codegen decorator/runtime-classifier mismatch, a two-switch env contradiction, a vitest include glob, or a stale ADR paragraph.

MINOR EVIDENCE NOTE (not verdict-driving): the report's footer states "40 review threads, 121 reviews, 138 issue comments"; the complete, untruncated raw payloads give 29 threads (45 thread comments), 113 reviews, 137 issue comments. The denominator the "nearly every" claim rests on is not reproducible from the pulled data as stated.
verdicts.correction: A single descriptive pattern — declared surfaces detached from their execution paths, records asserting what they do not derive — is the DOMINANT substance class in this window and is genuinely shared, not an artefact of compression: roughly 20 of 27 bot review-thread findings fit, nine of the ten table rows re-derive accurately from raw comments, and participants named the mechanism independently ("the ADR asserted a configuration fact instead of deriving it"). Two qualifications the report should carry. First, "nearly every" overstates: PR743's `statuses: write` privilege escalation and redelivery race, PR747's TOCTOU (the report's own top residual), PR749's `finally`-skip, and PR746's bootstrap-reporter and build-vs-buy findings are substantive in-window findings outside the class. Second, the class is one DESCRIPTION but not one CURE SURFACE: it decomposes into claim-not-derived (cure: derive at write time), enforcement-off-the-executed-path (cure: move the check onto the boot/codegen path plus regression), gate-green-against-the-wrong-artefact (cure: reachability and scope meta-checks), and correct-code-stale-record (cure: amend the doc) — the last of which points the opposite way from the second. PDR-135's STATED vs CHECKED ledger addresses roughly four of the ten instances; the remaining six needed code-level cures the ledger does not reach, so §4.4's "the meta-programme is validated by its own week" should read "the ledger is the right cure for one arm of a class whose other arms need their own instruments."

critique.verdict_on_solo_pass: "Strong synthesis, incomplete enumeration — and it failed on exactly the axis it diagnosed. §3.2 (the #747 dir-read TOCTOU), §3.3 (the suppressed-comments channel), §3.4 (re-pricing the review bottleneck) and §3.5 (the examples-survival assertion gap) are genuine, first-hand-verified contributions that a thread-only sweep would not have produced, and the §2 thesis — records that assert what they do not derive — is correct and better supported than the report knows: I found roughly six more verified instances it missed (#737's two, #738's ADR-218 pair, #731's validator count, #725's unpinned Ajv gate, #751's ADR-163 contradiction). But the report is not a safe picture of the board. It names the suppressed channel as a systematic blind spot and then drains 2 of the 11 PRs that carry it, leaving an undischarged privacy-retention gate on merged main (#738) and an ADR stating two incompatible deploy rules (#751) unsurfaced. It never touches check runs, so it reports #734 as a parked lane with a documented contract when the branch does not typecheck and its secret-scan is red. It drops an open CHANGES_REQUESTED PR (#737) from its own table while carrying a merged one (#754). Its scope note asserts a completeness its own §3.3 finding refutes, demonstrably, on #730 and #725. And its footer counts do not reconcile with the corpus they cite. On the proposals: #1 is the weakest of the five because it is a vigilance cure ('sweep suppressed comments once per PR at disposition time') in an estate whose owner principle is structure over vigilance. Two cheaper, more structural options were not considered — first, whether Copilot's suppression threshold is repo-configurable, since turning it off converts these into ordinary threads that every existing sweep already reads and costs no new practice; second, failing that, parsing the `<details>Suppressed comments</details>` block inside the existing agent-tools harvester so the sweep is mechanical rather than habitual. The same applies to the checks gap: pr-lifecycle already mandates harvesting all checks, so the report's own §5.1 falsifier ('if the misses were seat-specific process slips, the cure is seat habit, not the skill') is answerable from the report itself — it skipped a mandated step — and it never ran that test on its own method. Finally, proposals 2, 3 and 5 ticket three individual instances of one class; given ~sixteen verified instances now, the cheaper structural move is a single derive-at-render rule for the three asserted fields that recur most (blob SHA, base 'current main', last_updated/freshness frontmatter), which is what PDR-135's STATED-vs-CHECKED split is already reaching for."
